claims.text: Environmental Transmission Electron Microscopy (ETEM) with in-situ heating can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
In-situ heating ETEM will reveal structural mediators associated with thermodynamic contributions to thermal stability.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic nanoalloys.
The proposed ETEM experiment uses in-situ heating.
The proposed experimental conditions include vacuum and temperatures up to 1000°C.
Atomic-scale atomic arrangement and diffusion are the structural mediators of the observed thermal behavior.
Heating causes thermally activated diffusion and rearrangement of atoms in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit a 20% increase in thermal stability relative to a 500°C baseline.
Thermal stability is operationally measured as the temperature at which nanoparticle structure begins to degrade.
The baseline thermal-stability temperature of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles is 500°C.
The relevant experimental temperature range is 500–1000°C.
The exact temperature range and heating rate may affect the observed outcome.
ETEM spatial resolution may limit interpretation of the results.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 20% increase, but the hypothesis is only falsified below a 10% increase. An observed increase between 10% and 20% would fail the stated prediction without satisfying the falsification rule.
